title: Require Service Spine And Proof Topology
forbids: a standalone service outside its closed package and public client/service face, a missing root or module anchor, a second service spine, a service-root middleware directory with a barrel, nested child, or suffixed leaf, a module without a closed contract directory, one module-root router.ts composition face, and a closed router directory of named *.router.ts authorship leaves, a contract directory without index.ts, a router/index.ts second face, an open-ended or nested module contract, middleware, or router interior, an unclassified or nested model leaf, a model index.ts, a service proof corpus under src, a package-root service test outside the closed behavior, mechanics, integration, and support categories, a suite outside its admitted proof category, a suite under support, or a module-owned context, fresh implementer, host, error portal, or procedures container
why: A standalone service exposes one client beside one reusable service interior; standalone and API-embedded interiors then share one stable oRPC spine. Optional service-root middleware is a closed set of direct semantic leaves without a barrel. Each module exposes its contract through contract/index.ts, authors operations in named router/*.router.ts leaves, and composes those completed values through its sole public router.ts face. Optional module middleware retains its indexed catalog only when it exists. Root contract.ts and router.ts remain the service composition boundary, and root router.ts owns the sole aggregate router implementation. Optional model facts are classified as direct semantic leaves. The separate database blueprint owns database placement and interiors. Standalone proof lives in an optional package-root test tree so production source and production Nx inputs remain independent from behavior, mechanics, integration, and support assets.
remediate: Keep project.json, src, and tsconfig.json at a standalone service package root; keep client.ts beside service under src; and keep base.ts, contract.ts, impl.ts, modules, and router.ts at the service interior. When service-root middleware exists, keep direct simple kebab-case .ts leaves only; remove barrels, nesting, and role suffixes. In every module keep module.ts and router.ts beside required closed contract/ and router/ directories; keep the generic contract anchor in contract/index.ts, author operations in direct named router/*.router.ts leaves, and compose them through the generic router anchor in module-root router.ts. Remove router/index.ts. When module middleware exists, keep it in a closed middleware/ directory with index.ts and direct named *.ts leaves; remove the directory when no middleware exists. Classify optional model leaves directly under actors, dto, entities, errors, helpers, policy, ports, or prompts without index.ts files. Follow the separate database blueprint for the optional standalone service-root db child. Move standalone service proof out of src and into optional package-root test categories: behavior/modules/<module>/*.test.ts, mechanics/{client,contract,db}/*.test.ts, integration/*.test.ts, or support/{db,service,modules/<module>}/*.ts. Keep suites out of support; no empty category is required.
message: Service modules require one root router composition face over closed named router authorship leaves.
